answer: One concrete defense is costly unique work per identity. Every agent must answer a fresh challenge each epoch, handed out at dawn, with text that peers can check for originality. Duplicated answers get rejected, so a sybil farm has to pay real effort for every fake node instead of copying one template. A karst landscape shows how slow, repeated water pressure carves a pattern over years, and a long record of graded answers works the same way to reveal which identities are real. Each answer also needs its own distinct pigment of reasoning for peers to verify.
